mcqs.question: When aqueous solutions of silver nitrate (AgNO₃) and sodium chloride (NaCl) are mixed, a white solid appears. Which statement best explains this observation?

options.B: Formation of insoluble silver chloride (AgCl) precipitate
options.C: No chemical reaction occurs; the mixture remains clear
options.D: Formation of insoluble sodium chloride (NaCl) precipitate

mcqs.answer: Formation of insoluble silver chloride (AgCl) precipitate
mcqs.explanation: Ag⁺ ions combine with Cl⁻ ions to form AgCl, which is insoluble in water and appears as a white precipitate. Na⁺ and NO₃⁻ remain in solution as soluble NaNO₃. Options A and D describe soluble products, and option C ignores the reaction.

mcqs.question: A piece of zinc metal is placed into a solution of copper(II) sulfate. Which reaction correctly represents what happens?

options.C: No reaction occurs because zinc and copper are both metals

mcqs.explanation: Zinc is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper sulfate, forming zinc sulfate and metallic copper. Option B is not a balanced chemical equation, C is false, and D reverses the actual direction of displacement.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about metal reactivity with dilute hydrochloric acid is NOT correct?

options.A: Magnesium reacts vigorously, producing hydrogen gas.
options.B: Copper reacts vigorously, producing hydrogen gas.
options.C: Iron reacts slowly, producing hydrogen gas.
options.D: Zinc reacts readily, producing hydrogen gas.

mcqs.answer: Copper reacts vigorously, producing hydrogen gas.
mcqs.explanation: Copper is less reactive than hydrogen and does not react with dilute HCl under normal conditions. Magnesium, iron, and zinc are all more reactive than hydrogen and do react, making options A, C, and D correct statements.

mcqs.learning_point: Use metal reactivity to predict displacement
mcqs.question: Which metal can displace lead from an aqueous solution of lead nitrate (Pb(NO₃)₂)?
mcqs.explanation: Iron is higher than lead in the reactivity series, so it can displace lead ions, forming Fe(NO₃)₂ and metallic lead. Copper, silver, and gold are less reactive than lead and cannot cause displacement.

mcqs.question: Which of the following reactions is a double displacement (metathesis) reaction?
mcqs.explanation: In a double displacement reaction, cations and anions exchange partners. Reaction A shows Na⁺ swapping with Ag⁺, producing new ionic compounds. B is a single displacement, C is decomposition, and D is combustion.

mcqs.question: In a laboratory experiment, solutions of potassium iodide (KI) and lead(II) nitrate [Pb(NO₃)₂] are mixed. Which observation confirms that a precipitation reaction has taken place?

options.C: Increase in temperature of the mixture

mcqs.explanation: Pb²⁺ reacts with I⁻ to form lead(II) iodide, PbI₂, which is a yellow solid that precipitates out of solution. Gas evolution (A) and temperature change (C) are not characteristic of this reaction, and D indicates no reaction.

mcqs.question: Which of the following equations represents a displacement reaction?
mcqs.explanation: In a displacement reaction, a more reactive metal (Zn) replaces a less reactive metal (Cu) from its compound. Option A is synthesis, C is decomposition, and D is dissociation.

mcqs.question: Which metal is more reactive than magnesium (Mg) according to the reactivity series?
mcqs.explanation: Aluminium lies above magnesium in the reactivity series, meaning it can displace magnesium from its compounds. Copper, silver, and gold are less reactive than magnesium.
